lyrics:
[intro]
[verse]
The coffee’s getting cold in this city diner
The rain is drumming patterns on the glass
I’m staring at the map in the morning paper
Watching all the crowded hours pass
[chorus]
Oh, take me back to the red dirt highway
Where the pines lean low to hear the creek
I’m tired of the noise and the concrete shadow
And the empty words that strangers speak
[verse]
My boots are worn from the miles I’ve traveled
Since I left the porch light burning dim
There’s a ghost of laughter in the kitchen corner
And a hollow song that’s stuck within
[chorus]
Oh, take me back to the red dirt highway
Where the pines lean low to hear the creek
I’m tired of the noise and the concrete shadow
And the empty words that strangers speak
[bridge]
The moonlight hangs above the valley floor
I’m reaching for a key that fits the door
Of a house that hasn’t known my name for years
Drying up the salt of all these miles of tears
[chorus]
Oh, take me back to the red dirt highway
Where the pines lean low to hear the creek
I’m tired of the noise and the concrete shadow
And the empty words that strangers speak
[outro]
